Critique of Political Economy 1867
Karl Marx

Capital, Volume 1

Marx's magnum opus: A Critical Analysis of Capitalist Production (1867). Unveils the fundamental laws of motion of the capitalist mode of production, the fetishism of commodities, absolute and relative surplus value, the general law of capitalist accumulation, and the historical inevitability of proletarian revolution.

EN
Read Text →
Critique of Political Economy 1857
Karl Marx

Grundrisse: Outlines of the Critique of Political Economy

Marx's sprawling 1857-1858 research manuscripts for Capital. Explores the methodological dialectics of political economy, the historical specificity of bourgeois categories, the nature of money, and the contradictions of automated machinery and free time under communism.

EN
PDF · Read Text →
Critique of Political Economy 1916
V. I. Lenin

Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism

Written in Zurich in 1916 amidst the horrors of the First World War, Lenin analyzes the transformation of competitive industrial capitalism into monopoly finance capitalism, the global export of capital, the division of the earth among imperialist monopolies, and the epoch of proletarian revolution.

EN
Read Text →
Party, State & Revolution 1921
Amadeo Bordiga

Party and Class (1921)

Seminal theoretical text of the Italian Communist Left defining the revolutionary party as the conscious organ of the proletariat, refuting both bourgeois parliamentarism and syndicalist/workerist illusions of economic immediacy.

EN
Read Text →
Historical Materialism & Method 1859
Karl Marx

Preface to A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy

The classic summary of the materialist conception of history. Formulates the relationship between the economic base (relations of production corresponding to a given stage of the material forces) and the legal, political, and ideological superstructure.

EN
Read Text →
Party, State & Revolution 1922
Amadeo Bordiga

The Democratic Principle (1922)

A profound Marxist critique of bourgeois and inner-party democracy, demonstrating that communism rejects democracy as an eternal principle or moral fetish, subordinating organizational forms strictly to the historic programme and tasks of the proletarian revolution.

EN
Read Text →
Tactics & History of the Communist Left 1926
Left Faction of the Communist Party of Italy

The Lyon Theses

Drafted by Amadeo Bordiga and the Left Faction of the PCd'I for the 3rd Congress in Lyon, France (1926). A resolute defense of programmatic invariance, organic centralism, and communist discipline against Stalinist opportunism and democratic dilution.

EN
Read Text →
Tactics & History of the Communist Left 1922
Communist Party of Italy (PCd'I)

The Rome Theses

Theses on the Tactics of the Communist Party of Italy presented at the Second National Congress (Rome, March 1922). Synthesizes the Left's critique of democratic dilution, united-front maneuvers with social democracy, and opportunist compromises in the Third International.

EN
Read Text →
Party, State & Revolution 1917
V. I. Lenin

The State and Revolution

Written in hiding during August-September 1917, restoring the revolutionary Marxist doctrine of the state as an organ of class rule, the necessity of the dictatorship of the proletariat, the violent smashing of the bourgeois state apparatus, and the eventual withering away of the state under communism.

EN
Read Text →
Historical Materialism & Method 1845
Karl Marx

Theses on Feuerbach

Eleven foundational aphorisms drafted by Marx in 1845 outlining the departure of historical materialism from contemplative bourgeois materialism, culminating in the famous Thesis XI: 'The philosophers have only interpreted the world in various ways; the point is to change it.'

Party, State & Revolution 1920
Communist International (Comintern)

Theses on the Role of the Communist Party in the Proletarian Revolution (1920)

Adopted at the Second World Congress of the Communist International in Petrograd and Moscow, establishing the necessity of a centralized, disciplined communist vanguard party rooted in the working class to lead the overthrow of capitalism.

Critique of Political Economy 1865
Karl Marx

Value, Price and Profit

Marx's 1865 address to the First International confronting the reformist arguments of John Weston. A definitive exposition of the labour theory of value, the distinction between value and price, and the necessity of militant class struggle over the rate of surplus value.

EN
Read Text →
Critique of Political Economy 1849
Karl Marx

Wage Labour and Capital

An essential foundational critique of bourgeois political economy based on lectures delivered by Karl Marx to the German Workingmen's Club of Brussels in 1847. Explains the relationship between wages, labour-power as a commodity, capital accumulation, and the extraction of surplus value.
